title: Recs SIM Lab — UX prototyping and micro-interaction notes
content:
Purpose:
This is a working lab doc for an interactive simulation canvas (SIM Lab) inside the Optimize recommendations surface. The goal is to prototype micro-interactions and edge-case UX for exposing batching/caching/quantization suggestions to engineers and SREs, while keeping the console light enough for product teams to understand downstream quality/cost impact.

Scope and constraints (quick):
- Surface must show: suggestion, confidence / rationale, estimated token-cost delta, latency impact, and a simulated preview (synthetic requests).
- Must support comparing two or more recommendation variants (A/B style) inline.
- Should enable one-click apply, schedule rollout, and create a rollout policy (canary, % ramp).
- Telemetry hooks: preview-run id, suggestion-id, applied-by, rollback events.
- Backend: we assume inference advisor service provides `recs` with fields: suggestion_type, delta_cost_per_1k_tokens, est_lat_ms, confidence_score, affected_routes.
- UI must accommodate missing data: unknown cost/lat -> show "estimate unavailable" plus link to why.

Audience / personas (for microflows):
- Platform Engineer (SRE): cares about latency SLO, throughput, and rollback controls. Wants a compact view with keyboard-friendly actions.
- ML Engineer: wants fidelity of quality estimates and quick A/B preview on eval prompt set.
- Product Engineer: cares about overall cost impact and user-visible output regressions; wants example outputs and severity indicator.

Wireframe ideas (micro-interactions called out):
1) Suggestion Card (compact):
   - Left: icon for type (batching/caching/quantize) + short title (e.g., "Prefix cache: enabled for /v1/generate")
   - Middle: three-line summary: confidence (heat gauge), est-cost-delta (green/red), est-p99-latency-change (ms).
   - Right: primary actions: "Run preview" (▶), "Quick apply" (bolt), overflow (⋯) for schedule, annotate, or open detailed simulation.
   - Micro-interaction: hover over cost shows a sparklines mini-chart of hourly cost estimate; clicking opens a cost breakdown flyout.

2) Detailed Simulation Panel (modal / right rail):
   - Top: headline with suggestion id and hypothesis text (why this helps).
   - Middle: split pane — left: metric projections (table + chart for token throughput, cost, latency across 7 days), right: sample-request sandbox showing before/after outputs for 3 representative prompts taken from the user's eval collection.
   - Bottom: action bar: "Apply to route", "Schedule rollout", "Save as preset", "Discard".
   - Micro-interaction: sample outputs are live-run (synthetic) with an ephemeral preview-run id. Toggle between raw tokens and formatted output.

3) Compare mode (side-by-side):
   - Allow selecting 2-3 suggestions to compare. For each: show delta-cost, latency, quality-bucket (no-regression / minor / potential-regression), and a diff view of sample replies.
   - Keyboard: left/right to move between suggestions; space to play sample request.

Backlog items and acceptance criteria (rough priority):
- OPT-1001: Basic suggestion card list (MVP) — shows 10 recs, with cost/lat/confidence. Accept if list loads in < 800ms and cards include three metrics.
- OPT-1002: Preview runner integration — run synthetic prompts against chosen rec(s). Accept if preview completes within 5s for up to 3 prompts and preview-run ID is logged.
- OPT-1003: One-click apply + rollback hook — creates a rollout with default canary of 5% for 1 hour. Accept if create returns rollout-id and UI shows live health.
- OPT-1004: Comparison table — compare 2 recs side-by-side with sample diff. Accept if diffs load and diff UI highlights token-level changes.
- OPT-1005: Cost estimator fallback UI — show "est. unavailable" and link to diagnostic page when backend returns null.

Quality / safety guardrails to surface: (product and SRE must see these pre-apply)
- Potential quality regression flag: if model-run leads to >5% change in BLEU/ROUGE on protected eval set, mark as "review required".
- Sensitive input detection: if sample outputs contain PII or policy-matching text, then disable quick apply and require a manual review ticket.
- Quantization warning: when suggestion reduces precision (e.g., 16->8 bit), show explicits: "expected output variance: low/medium/high" and link to quantization QA checklist.

Telemetry and observability fields (UX notes):
- Attach suggestion_id, preview_run_id, applied_rollout_id, user_id to each action.
- Surface live SLO impact chart during rollout: p50/p95/p99 and error-rate.
- Allow clicking a metric to open trace logs in Console -> Tracing.

Microcopy and small copy fragments (quick list):
- Suggestion card confidence label: "High / Medium / Low (reason: sample diversity)"
- Quick apply CTA: "Apply to route — start canary"
- Preview button: "Run sample preview (no commit)"
- Cost tooltip: "Estimated token cost change per 1k requests — calculated from last 7 days of traffic profile"

Design decisions and alternatives (open):
- Inline vs modal detailed view: inline right-rail gives more context and faster keyboard flow; modal is simpler but breaks continuity. Lean toward right-rail.
- Aggressiveness of default canary: default 5% seems safe for most orgs; enterprise customers should have a saved policy override.
- Show absolute cost vs percent change: show both; percent is easier to scan, absolute is required for billing teams.

Edge-case notes and TODOs (scratchpad):
- If suggestion affects multiple routes, show aggregated impact and allow split-apply (per-route toggle).
- For very high-confidence cache suggestions that require infra changes (e.g., redis keyspace), surface a precondition list and provide infra ticket template.
- UX for "no-data" customers: show guided checklist to opt-in to usage profiling so estimates can be provided.
- Investigate a "dry-run" toggle that runs previews with reduced model capacity (simulated latency) to reduce cost.

Rollout plan (high level):
- Phase 0: internal alpha to Optimize team + one SRE pilot (2 weeks) — aim: validate preview-run performance and telemetry.
- Phase 1: beta in Console -> Optimize for 3 customers on Dedicated (1 month) — collect cost/quality metrics + feedback.
- Phase 2: public launch in Console (gradual feature flag rollout) with deep links to docs and quantization QA checklist.

Open questions for engineering:
- What is the SLA on preview-run? can we guarantee under 5s for 3 prompts at 1x sequence length?
- How do we version suggestion schemas? need a migration plan if advisor returns new fields.
- Is there an existing rollout API endpoint that supports percent ramps and automatic rollback on SLO breach? (link to infra API needed)

Next steps (this sprint):
- Design: create 3 fidelity wireframes for suggestion card / detailed panel / compare mode (Priya) — due 11/11.
- FE: stub suggestion-list + right-rail detail with static JSON (Ethan) — due 11/18.
- BE: contract for preview-run endpoint + telemetry schema (Diego) — API proposal 11/15.
- PM: capture acceptance criteria for OPT-1001..1005 and add to grooming board (Ava) — done 11/05.

Notes to self / brainstorming fragments (messy):
- "maybe show recommended quantization level as a slider? but risk of exposing too much to non-ML users"
- "quickapply should open confirmation with key metrics — avoid accidental apply"
- "color coding: green for cost-down, orange for latency-up moderate, red for regression risk"

Appendix: example JSON shape we expect from Advisor (sketch) — for BE handoff: 
- suggestion_id: string
- type: [batch, cache, quantize]
- short_title: string
- confidence: float
- delta_cost_per_1k: float|null
- est_p95_latency_ms: float|null
- affected_routes: [string]
- sample_prompts: [string]
- quality_estimate: {metric_name:float}  <-- UI note: we will show a small set, but map to a single severity label

This doc is intentionally messy — use it as the source of truth for the SIM Lab proto grooming meeting. Update with links to new wireframes and prototype embeds as they exist.

Quick links (workbench):
- mockups: https://figma.com/redwood-optimize/sim-lab
- grooming board: https://linear.app/redwood/board/optimize/
